text:
sara: seeing a small spike of GPU pod evictions in eu-west-2 tonight, all on the same node pool. evict reason from kubelet is the network health probe failing repeatedly. not seeing CPU/mem pressure. :thinking:

mike: interesting — any common NIC type / kernel? RDMA enabled on that pool?

sara: yes it's the RDMA-enabled partition (A100s). SR-IOV + Mellanox drivers. only ~6 pods evicted across 3 nodes so far.

jia: also noticed increased east-west packet reordering in perf dashboards around the same time window. could be causing probe timeouts.

sara: here's the kubelet log excerpt from one node: 
```
Mar 14 02:12:05 k8s-gpu-12 kubelet[1234]: network probe failed: probe "udp/icmp" -> timeout after 5s, consecutive failures: 4
Mar 14 02:12:06 k8s-gpu-12 kubelet[1234]: eviction controller: marking pod as evicted: reason=NetworkHealthProbeFailed, grace=0
Mar 14 02:12:06 k8s-gpu-12 kubelet[1234]: evicted pod: gpu-training-xyz-0 (namespace: ml-prod)
```
\nmike: netprobe is configured with 2s poll and 3 failures threshold here (IIRC). with RDMA and occasional fragmentation/reassembly latency that could be marginal.

jia: also saw ICMP 'frag needed' logs on the NIC: `ip frag needed mtu=1500` while our overlay expects 9000. looks like somewhere on path MTU is getting stuck at 1500 for certain flows.

sara: that'd explain intermittent probe failures. overlay MTU is 9000 for RDMA pool; if an intermediate hop drops jumbo frames it causes fragmentation and sometimes the probe's UDP/ICMP doesn't get back in time.

mike: possible causes: 1) kernel update on host or switch firmware fallback, 2) recent Calico ipip/encap change, 3) ECMP path asymmetry for certain dst ports. any recent infra churn?

infra-bot: deploy: calico-daemonset v3.26.1 promoted to eu-west-2 at 01:58 UTC (by @infra-deploy).

sara: thanks infra-bot — uplift matches timing. mike, can you check the calico config in eu-west-2? especially encapsulation mode and MTU auto-detection.

mike: on it. pulling the daemonset:
```
$ kubectl -n kube-system get ds calico -o yaml
# note: FelixConfig: ipipMode: Always, vethMTU: 1500
```
\nmike: confirmed Felix vethMTU set to 1500 because calico auto-detected host MTU after the deploy. our RDMA nodes should remain 9000. looks like the deploy accidentally flipped detection behavior on RDMA hosts.

jia: that would cause overlay interfaces to advertise 1500, causing fragmentation for jumbo flows. short flows (like control plane) okay; packets with large payloads (our net-probe UDP tests with 4k payload) could timeout.

sara: immediate mitigation: raise kubelet probe thresholds to avoid evictions during noisy windows and roll back felix MTU change. can we do a quick canary?

mike: propose steps: 1) patch calico daemonset in eu-west-2 to force vethMTU: 9000 for rdma node pool (label selector), 2) increase kubelet net probe failure threshold to 6 for the RDMA pool via node-config (or daemonset kubelet-wrapper) temporarily, 3) monitor for evictions for 30m, 4) roll forward config if green.

jia: agree. small note: kubelet flags might require restart of kubelet process — plan a rolling restart of kubelets on the affected nodes. keep one node untouched to preserve capacity.

sara: can you run the calico patch and increase kubelet threshold as a quick patch? I can coordinate the kubelet restarts if needed.

mike: applying calico change now to rdma pool (selector: hw-type=rdma):
```
kubectl -n kube-system patch ds calico --type='json' -p='[{
 "op":"add", "path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/-", "value": {"name":"FELIX_VETH_MTU", "value":"9000"}
}]'
```
\nmike: patched; pods will restart across nodes. I also created a temporary ConfigMap for kubelet: `kubelet-netprobe-tuning` with failures=6. applying to rdma nodes via node-config daemonset.

infra-bot: action: calico-ds rolling restart started (eu-west-2).

sara: monitoring dashboards now — dropping error rate on netprobe back to baseline on node-12 as its calico pod restarted.

jia: evictions stopped on node-12. node-13/14 still showing intermittent failures but improving.

mike: rolling out kubelet threshold config now. will restart kubelet on node-13 after calico pod is ready.

sara: after both patches and kubelet bump, no new evictions for 40 minutes. good sign.

mike: follow-ups: 1) revert temporary kubelet tuning once we're confident, 2) add a Calico preflight to our deploy pipeline to avoid MTU auto-detection flips on special pools, 3) update runbook to include RDMA MTU checklist and our probe thresholds per node-type.

jia: also add a metric for 'probe failure reason' to surface fragmentation vs unreachable so we can distinguish path MTU vs blackhole.

sara: agree. I'll open the runbook PR and tag you both. thanks for quick turnaround — saved a few long-running training jobs. :relieved: 

mike: np. will follow up with a short postmortem entry and the calico change diff.

jia: nice catch on the deployment timing. cc @networking for FYI. :eyes:

sara: closing thread, keeping monitors for 2 hours then will mark incident resolved if green. :white_check_mark:
